Hold off on adding new money to your taxable brokerage account right now. Prioritize **reinforcing your cash buffers and protecting your tax reserve** to handle income volatility and upcoming quarterly tax obligations.

### Why holding cash is the right priority right now

- **Upcoming Q2 estimated tax deadline** — The second-quarter federal estimated tax payment is due on **June 15, 2026**. Your **$18,500** in the Ally Tax Reserve Savings should remain strictly cordoned off for quarterly payments and your year-end tax liability.
- **Thin net business operating cushion** — Your Bluevine Business Checking balance is **$7,420**, but you have **$6,395** in statement balances across your Chase Ink ($5,210) and Amex Blue Business Plus ($1,185). Paying these off leaves an operating buffer of roughly **$1,025**, which is vulnerable if a client invoice is delayed.
- **Personal runway needs reinforcement** — With monthly living costs averaging roughly **$3,200** (rent at $2,100, health insurance at $415, utilities, groceries, and medical), your **$9,650** Capital One checking balance provides about **3 months** of coverage. For solo consultants with variable revenue, a **6- to 9-month reserve ($19,000–$28,000)** is the recommended target to absorb dry spells without selling market assets at a loss.
- **Tax-advantaged room before taxable** — You already hold **$48,000** in your Fidelity brokerage and **$12,500** in crypto. Any future surplus should first flow to tax-advantaged buckets — such as maxing your Fidelity HSA (the 2026 self-only limit is **$4,400**) or your retirement accounts — before adding to taxable brokerage.

### Recommended action sequence

1. **Protect the tax reserve** — Keep the Ally savings balance dedicated exclusively to estimated quarterly tax payments and tax prep.
2. **Rebuild the business checking buffer** — Retain at least 1–2 months of recurring business overhead in checking after paying credit card balances before drawing profits.
3. **Build personal emergency savings toward 6 months** — Move extra personal cash above monthly bill-pay needs into a separate high-yield savings account until you reach ~$19,000.
4. **Fund HSA and retirement accounts next** — Max out your tax-advantaged vehicles to reduce taxable income before directing new dollars to your taxable brokerage.
